author: PokerFace
body:
Guys, it's going to happen unless we do something to prevent this from happening. All the chaos of people leaving, it's going to cause too much stress. At this point, it is vital things get done quickly and properly. Now is the time for change to happen. If change doesn't come, nothing will be able to make up for our losses. All these suggestion threads, it is time for them to actually be listened to. Not only listened to but, actually put into effect. The community is saying what needs to be done. What needs to be done has to happen. It is extremely vital that we all do our part now. Whether it's responding to reports, moderating the forums or, simply organizing an event, it has to happen soon. If it doesn't happen soon, this community is going to start to diminish. Especially now because , many staff are leaving us. It is time to do our part. Whether we are a player or a moderator, we have to support one another to get us out of this trench. 

-PokerFace

replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
This "trench"? Sorry, but I'm gonna side with the ones saying you're acting slightly melodramatic. Personally, these circumstances are by no means irremediable, much less grave or pernicious — it's part of the cycle of the staff team that I've come to understand (somewhat) after being here for ten months.

Typically, an important staff member, such as an administrator, abdicates from their position, galvanizing an initially reluctant wave of further demotions and resignations. This deficiency in the member count of the staff team is soon counterbalanced by a new session of staff applications and interviews, among other events. Shortly thereafter, literally dozens of new moderators are put on trial and we appear to have a surfeit of them. Over the subsequent months they gradually start to decrease in number until we encounter another occurrence that mandates taking action... though I'm sure you knew all this already. In that case, I don't know why I'm wasting my time reiterating...

If this is just part of the perennial pattern, then we'll be fine, right? Pretty much. The staff team is already hard at work to completely fill in the gaps left by recent incidents, not to mention the upcoming update and experimentation of "hand-picked staff" later this month (if I remember correctly).

I'm not usually one to think optimistically, but come on — the server will pull through and burgeon, and everything will fall into place; just have some faith and a bit of patience.
